title: Applying a Single Payment Across Several Placed Consumer Accounts
content:
Cashiering standard for **Placed Consumer Accounts**: how one payment from a consumer who owes more than one placed account is divided among those accounts, and what happens to any amount left over.

## Standard

**1. Consumer's direction.** When a consumer who holds more than one open placed account makes a single payment, the payment is split and applied account by account following the consumer's direction. The consumer's direction prevails even when it names an account that is not the oldest.

**2. Accounts that can receive a portion.** Under the multi-account allocation, a payment portion is applied only to a placed account whose status is placed, validation period, active, arranged or hardship hold. No portion is ever applied to an account that has a dispute on its case history with no verification mailing answering it, even when that dispute did not place a hold. The status and the case history are read from Ridgeline's records for the account.

**3. No direction given.** When the consumer gives no direction, the payment is applied first to the eligible account with the earliest first delinquency date, then to the next earliest, each account receiving no more than its balance due. When two accounts share a first delinquency date, the account with the smaller balance due comes first.

**4. One open account.** A consumer who holds only one open placed account may direct a voluntary payment to it even while it is in dispute hold.

**5. Amount left over.** Any amount left after every account named or ordered has been brought to zero is not held as a credit and is not moved to an account the consumer did not name. It is refunded to the consumer as an overpayment refund booked against the account that received the last applied portion, pointing back to that payment.

**6. Limits.** Payments are never applied across consumers, and never to accounts that are paid in full, settled in full or returned to client.

## Order of application without direction

| Rank | Rule |
|---|---|
| First | Eligible account with the earliest first delinquency date |
| Tie on that date | The account with the smaller balance due comes first |
| Each account | Receives no more than its balance due |
| After the last eligible account reaches zero | The remainder is refunded against the account that received the last applied portion |

## Hypothetical worked allocation

*All accounts, dates and amounts are invented.* A consumer pays $500.00 and gives no direction. The consumer's open accounts are:

| Account | Status | First delinquency date | Balance due | Unanswered dispute on file |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | active | 2024-03-01 | $200.00 | No |
| B | arranged | 2024-03-01 | $150.00 | No |
| C | dispute hold | 2023-11-15 | $100.00 | Yes |
| D | active | 2023-12-01 | $90.00 | Yes, a phone dispute that placed no hold |

C is excluded by its status and D by its unanswered dispute. A and B share the earliest remaining date, so B, with the smaller balance, comes first: B receives $150.00 and A receives $200.00. The $150.00 left over is refunded to the consumer against account A, the account that received the last applied portion.

## Basis questions

**May the consumer send the whole payment to the newest account?** Yes. The consumer's direction prevails even when it names an account that is not the oldest, provided that account can receive a portion under paragraph 2.

**Can a leftover be parked on the account as a credit for next month?** No. It is refunded as described in paragraph 5.
